newsitem.title: USA: Quaker declines comment on Snapple report.
newsitem.headline: Quaker declines comment on Snapple report.

text.p: Quaker Oats Co on Friday declined to comment on a published report that it is seeking to sell its Gatorade sports drink and its Snapple beverage business.
"I will simply tell you that it is our policy not to comment on rumors and speculation," Quaker spokesman Ronald Bottrell said.
The Wall Street Journal reported Friday that several big companies are said to be weighing bids for Quaker's entire beverage business, which could fetch between $3.0 billion and $4.0 billion.
The newspaper said that while negotiations have not been announced, investment bankers, beverage industry analysts and others close to Quaker independently confirmed the substance of the talks.
Gatorade is Quaker's largest branding, expected to top $1.0 billion in sales in the United States alone this year.

Snapple, which Quaker bought for about $1.8 billion including transaction costs about two years ago, has not met the company's expectations. Quaker has said it expects Snapple to post an operating loss this year, although a narrower loss than last year.
Quaker shares were up two at 38.
